title: Non default VRF removal fails due to VRF references existing
author: vsenchyshyn

comments.author: anshuv-mfst
comments.body: @prsunny could you please look into this issue, thanks.

comments.author: msosyak
comments.body:
@prsunny I have faced this issue too on the SONiC master image. From my investigation, the issue is with default routes. When we delete VRF swss tries to delete all routes in it but default routes(with mask 0, added by BGP) are not deleted. the Are updated with DROP nexthop and due to that we still have a reference(to VRF)  that should be removed when all routes in that vrf are removed.
Here are the refs to the code:
https://github.com/Azure/sonic-swss/blob/a44e6513556cfed7de1b70690db90cc09fcef666/orchagent/routeorch.cpp#L1909
https://github.com/Azure/sonic-swss/blob/a44e6513556cfed7de1b70690db90cc09fcef666/orchagent/routeorch.cpp#L1953
https://github.com/Azure/sonic-swss/blob/a44e6513556cfed7de1b70690db90cc09fcef666/orchagent/routeorch.cpp#L2033

Not sure how this should be fixed. I have two idea: 
1. Apply the logic mentioned above only when `vrf_id == gVirtualRouterId` (Likely hotfix then the solution)
2. Create default routes to blackhole on VRF creation, updated it if needed(BGP announce), set back to blackhole on route deletion, and then delete on VRF  deletion.

**What I did**

1. Remove default prefix in non-default VRF instead of setting it to blackhole
2. Initialize `m_overlay_nexthops` in overloaded constructor. 


**Why I did it**
To fix https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/issues/6504

1. To remove default routes in non default VRF
2. To avoid garbage in `m_overlay_nexthops`. 

**How I verified it**
1. Add t0 topology
2. Load config generated by this test vrf/test_vrf.py::TestVrfDeletion::test_vrf1_neigh_after_restore
3. `sudo config vrf del Vrf1`
4. `redis-cli -n 6 keys "*VRF*"`
5. check that there is entries only for Vrf2. e.g:
```
1) "VRF_OBJECT_TABLE|Vrf2"
2) "VRF_TABLE|Vrf2"
```

**Details if related**
